_doc: Drive 9 whole-character round 5, ESCALATION 3 (recombine): the alternative lever mix, rendered on lanes/drive9n.blend (route F3 variant N: A's smaller bells, L's tabard and B's hair). r5_model.json plus the far bell blown back behind the haft, so the silhouette opens where the critics found it clogged (elbow-hip, waist, body-haft). Paired with r5x_finish.json (a lower key). Never baked; pose files never edited.

why.circlet: Removed (face critic, round 3: 'the gold diadem sits on the brow line, so the eyes are pinned under a heavy gold bar and the face is squeezed into the lower third'; 'the control proves the bare fringe reads better'; attractiveness: 'use F's bare-head look as default').
why.hair_volume: Face critic (head and hair 5): 'cut the crown scale back to 1.0-1.05 and put the volume into the sides and ends'. Every hair part: x1.03 at the crown (z 1.88), rising to x1.10 at the ear line (z 1.62) and below, about the head's vertical axis. The five fringe clumps (04-08) are left as they are, as in round 3.
why.idle: Body critic (round 3): 'best composite: R2 idle torso and arms + control legs'. Round 2's idle patch whole (hips 6.5/19.5/5.2, torso bend -15.6/-6.5, upper chest 8, near hand on the hip [-0.21, 0.09, 1.10], elbow pole [-0.9, 1.0, 1.3], near bell x0.78 blown back, tabard straight) without its free-knee pole, so the legs are the figure-pose lane's own lambda (the control's). Round 3's spine tilt -26, chest lift and glaive slide are dropped: they pulled the glaive arm's upper arm across the bust (a rev-3.5 Never).
why.head_tilt: Face critic (attractiveness): 'a head tilt of 5-10 degrees toward camera'. Tilt 16 -> 9 and chin 10 -> 5: round 2's 16/10 foreshortened the face from above and pushed the eyes down under the brow.
why.ribcage: Body critic (body 5): 'the ribcage is short, so the bust sits almost on the navel; lengthen the ribcage 1-2 px at 144'. The spine bone is scaled x1.14 along its length and the chest bone counter-scaled, so only the waist between the pelvis and the ribcage stretches (applied after IK; the hands move under 1 px).
why.back: Body and face critics: 'the control back (F) is the one to copy'; 'keep the head turned to camera over the shoulder, as the control does'. Round 2/3's look patches are dropped, so the look is the pose file's own (amount 1.0, max 85). The near bell sleeve covered the waist and hip ('the sleeve and hair still cover the back'): scaled x0.72 and blown forward harder. Round 3's hair to the far side is kept. Same ribcage stretch as the idle.
why.q: Body critic (posing 10): 'q is a static stand with the vertical glaive covering the body; replace q with D's kick'. Round 2's Q patch (rear foot at 0.32 m, knee pole down, camera yaw 35) replaces round 3's planted stand. Round 3's glaive direction (+0.18, about 10 degrees to her left) is kept on top, so the haft stands beside her face rather than through it (PS-P31: both hands stay on the haft).
why.tabard: Kept from rounds 2-3 (x1.3 at the waist to x1.65 at the hem).
why.pin: Face critic (round 4, head and hair 4): 'every ref head has a memorable top silhouette (ears, horns, a hat or a hair accessory); ours has none now that the diadem is gone ... add a small head-top signature that sits in the hairline, never across the brow: a gold stained-glass rosette or veil pin at the crown on the far side, 3-4 px, with a short veil or ribbon trailing off it'. r5_blender.pin: a 3.4 cm rosace (gold rim, glass, glasscore: the weapon disc's materials) on the hair's surface at azimuth 25 / elevation 58 (upper crown, toward the model's left = the far side in the idle's 45 deg view), two 13 cm veil tails with V cuts falling back and down. Trials: azimuth 75 put it edge-on and behind the hair (2 gold px, raw/r5_t1); a tail laid straight down the tangent plane from the front crown fell over the face.
why.idle_r5: Body critic (round 4, posture 9 / posing 10 / body 5): 'lift the chest and lengthen the neck 2 px; tilt the head 6-8 deg, chin down'; 'pull the near sleeve behind the hip so a 3-4 px waist notch of background shows'. Upper chest 8 -> 11, look tilt 9 -> 7 and chin 5 -> 6, neck_l 1.15 (d9_blender --neck-l), the near bell x0.78 -> x0.72 and blown back harder (g 0.5 -> 0.4, wind [-0.3, 1.2, 0.2] -> [-0.5, 1.6, 0.3]).
why.x_mix: ESCALATION 3: rebuild from a different lever mix. Round 4's body critic: 'silhouette clogged: the far drape fills the space between body and haft, the near sleeve fills the waist'; the outfit critic credited the big bells for mass. Mix X takes the mass from the tabard and hair (F3 N) instead of the bells, blows the far bell back behind the haft (sleeve_L g 0.4, wind [0.4, 1.8, 0.2]) and keeps the near bell at x0.85 of N's smaller bell; the finish goes lower-key (r5x_finish.json).
